items.title: Ember Analysis Credits Electric Vehicles With $20bn Oil Import Saving
items.summary: The energy think tank Ember estimates that battery-electric vehicles in oil-importing nations displaced 200 million barrels of crude oil between March and August 2026.
items.content_html:
AI-assisted summary — A concise view to help navigate news and sources. Learn more

Electric vehicles in oil-importing countries displaced an estimated 200 million barrels of crude oil between March and August 2026, worth about $20bn, according to the energy think tank Ember. The analysis frames battery-electric cars not only as a means to cut emissions but also as a tool to reduce dependence on imported crude oil, a core concern of sustainable mobility policy. Ember quantifies the aggregate benefit for economies that import fossil fuels, not an identical saving for every motorist.

The estimate attributes the largest share to China, which avoided $14bn in oil imports. European Union member states contributed another $3.1bn, chiefly through Germany and France. In Denmark, where the electric fleet is already established, Ember says electric cars displace an amount of oil equivalent to 13% of national consumption on an annual basis. These figures are presented as estimates of crude oil not purchased because electric vehicles replaced internal combustion engine cars.

The analysis also tracks market share. In 2026, 15 countries surpassed the United States in the share of sales of fully electric vehicles for the first time, including India, Brazil, Italy, Malaysia and New Zealand. The comparison covers battery-electric vehicles (BEVs) and excludes plug-in hybrids. In the US, BEVs accounted for 6% of sales in the first eight months of 2026, after federal support for electric mobility was reduced in 2025. In India, the BEV share exceeded the US figure every month from April. Brazil is gaining ground through domestic market growth and expanded national production capacity, according to Ember. The think tank says 49 of 56 monitored countries now have a BEV market share above the United States.

Global sales of battery-electric cars rose 11% in the first eight months of 2026 compared with the same period in 2025, Ember reports. Plug-in hybrids fell 12% and internal combustion engine vehicles declined 6%. Excluding China and the United States, global BEV sales grew by about 45% year-on-year. The article notes that Italy’s position relative to the United States does not by itself describe the maturity of its domestic market; absolute volumes, registration trends and the pace of fleet growth also matter.

items.title: Zero DS Travels 436.5 km on One Charge in Guinness-Certified Run
items.summary: A production Zero DS fitted with an optional Power Tank covered 436.5 km from the France–Italy border to the Mediterranean coast, exceeding the previous electric motorcycle record by about 125 km.
items.content_html:
AI-assisted summary — A concise view to help navigate news and sources. Learn more

An electric motorcycle covered 436.5 km on a single charge, a distance its maker submitted for Guinness World Records verification. The run speaks directly to the battery capacity and charging questions that shape electric mobility, although it was planned to maximise efficiency rather than to reproduce ordinary riding conditions.

The machine was a production Zero DS, unmodified but fitted with the optional Power Tank, which raises battery capacity from 15.6 kWh to 19.2 kWh. Jelle Verstaen rode it from the Alps on the France–Italy border to the Mediterranean coast. The route avoided motorways and favoured few stops; where road and limits allowed, the group held a cruising speed of about 52 km/h, and mountain descents let regenerative braking recover energy. The final 100 km were ridden in heavy rain.

The distance was tracked by GPS and checked under Guinness World Records procedures, the reports state. It exceeds the previous record of 310.689 km by more than 125 km, an improvement of roughly 40 per cent.

Two other Zero riders also passed the old mark. Louis Renaud, a customer present initially as an independent observer, rode his own SR/S for 350 km and stopped with 4 per cent of charge remaining. Jenny Brookes, the company's Senior Global Brand Manager, covered 384 km on a DSR/X before exhausting the battery.

Both reports note the limits. Zero declares an urban range of 249 km for the standard DS. The Vaielettrico report frames the record as a challenge to an autonomy bias, the habit of judging electric vehicles on maximum distance alone, while L'Espresso notes that range depends on speed, temperature, gradients, riding style and load, and that planning a journey remains necessary.

items.title: Paris and Berlin Near Deal to Relax EU Car Emissions Target
items.summary: A reported Franco-German bargain would soften the EU's 2035 carbon-dioxide target for new cars in return for “Made in Europe” rules on electric-vehicle subsidies and public procurement.
items.content_html:
AI-assisted summary — A concise view to help navigate news and sources. Learn more

France and Germany are reportedly closing on a bargain over the European Union's carbon-dioxide rules for new cars: Paris is said to be ready to soften the 2035 target in exchange for Berlin's backing for strict “Made in Europe” conditions on subsidies and public procurement for electric vehicles and batteries. The reported trade goes to the centre of the bloc's emissions rules for cars, because the 2035 requirement determines how quickly carmakers must move away from combustion engines, and procurement conditions would shape where the electric cars and batteries that replace them are built.

The European Commission has already proposed easing that target to a 90 per cent cut in emissions rather than 100 per cent against 2021, La Verità reports. The two governments are said to want a further ten points, to at least 80 per cent, and five years instead of three to reach the 2030 intermediate objective. Any understanding would still need a qualified majority in the Council and the European Parliament, which votes in plenary in November. France had been in a minority of seven states, with Spain, that blocked an earlier dilution; La Verità says the balance of forces has since shifted.

The pressure behind the talks is visible in the industry's figures. In the third quarter of 2026 Volkswagen delivered 14.3 per cent fewer vehicles, its steepest fall in more than four years, with its Chinese market down 38.5 per cent. Mercedes lost 31 per cent in China, while Porsche fell 33 per cent over nine months. German output stands at 3.03 million cars, 15 per cent below 2019, and the sector employs 691,500 people, the lowest since 2005, after 42,300 jobs went in a year. La Verità reports that Chinese brands' share rose from 5.5 to 11.7 per cent in twelve months and that the plug-in hybrid share went from 2 per cent in 2024 to 25 per cent, neither figure given with a stated base or territory; in Italy, it says, Chinese vehicles went from 6.5 per cent in 2025 to 13.7 per cent in August 2026.

Brussels has also pressed Beijing, asking Chinese manufacturers to halve exports of hybrids and plug-ins to Europe, according to Rinnovabili, which reports that Changan Automobile plans 180,000 cars a year in Europe by 2028 and 350,000 by 2030, with a first European-built vehicle as early as 2027. Stéphane Séjourné, the European Commissioner for Industry, said at a Politico competitiveness summit in Paris that a Franco-German compromise would break the political stalemate, particularly inside the European Parliament. Renault, Volkswagen and Stellantis together build more than 60 per cent of Europe's cars, Rinnovabili notes.

items.title: BYD unveils seven-seat Atto 8 electric SUV at Paris show for Europe
items.summary: The 115 kWh seven-seater, quoted at up to 653 km on the WLTP combined cycle, is due in European markets in 2027, with prices not yet announced.
items.content_html:
AI-assisted summary — A concise view to help navigate news and sources. Learn more

BYD chose the Paris motor show for the European premiere of the Atto 8, a seven-seat electric sport utility vehicle presented as a showcase of battery, charging and cabin technology. It sits within the electric-vehicle strand of sustainable mobility coverage: a battery-powered model whose reported specifications concern drivetrain output, battery capacity, range and charging time. One report frames it as supporting BYD's ambitions in the higher end of the market.

The Atto 8 measures 5,040 mm long, 1,996 mm wide and 1,760 mm tall and uses BYD's second-generation Blade Battery, with a stated capacity of 115 kWh in both versions. The Design RWD carries a rear electric motor of 340 kW — quoted as 462 CV — with 365 Nm of torque and a 0 to 100 km/h time of eight seconds; its WLTP combined range is given as 653 km. The Excellence AWD adds a front motor for a system output of 570 kW, quoted as 775 CV, and 775 Nm, cutting the 0 to 100 km/h time to 4.6 seconds; on the same WLTP combined basis its range is given as 602 km, with battery capacity unchanged.

The model brings Flash Charging to Europe on a BYD for the first time. Both accounts give the same figure, taking the battery from 10 per cent to 97 per cent in nine minutes; one adds that this applies at charging stations of 400 kW and above. No prices have been announced.

The luggage compartment holds 270 litres with all seven seats in use, rising to 1,960 litres with the second and third rows folded, alongside a 136-litre front compartment. Front seats are heated, ventilated and fitted with a massage function, and the same functions are available on the two outer seats of the second row; three-zone climate control is standard and rear passengers have a dedicated panel for the air conditioning. One report says all seats are trimmed in leather. The Atto 8 is due in European markets in the first six months of 2027 on one account, and in the first part of 2027 on the other.

Stella Li, BYD's executive vice president, said the Atto 8 "represents in an optimal way how we transform research and innovation into concrete solutions". The Paris show also hosted the European debut of the BYD Shark DMO, a super-hybrid pick-up due to launch in European markets in the coming months.

items.title: Renault unveils electric E-Space Concept as a reinvention of its Espace minivan
items.summary: The French carmaker's Paris Motor Show concept revives the Espace formula with a glazed cabin, rotating seats and steer-by-wire, though no production version has been confirmed.
items.content_html:
AI-assisted summary — A concise view to help navigate news and sources. Learn more

Renault unveiled the E-Space Concept, an electric people carrier, at the Paris Motor Show, presenting it as a modern-day take on the Espace minivan it introduced in 1984 and as "a real alternative to SUVs and saloons". The concept is not in production, and the supplied coverage carried no range, battery or charging figures. Renault frames the design around "travel and family mobility in the electric age"; the sources document packaging and cabin design, not measured environmental outcomes.

At 4,700 mm long, 2,020 mm wide and 1,670 mm tall, it is close in size to the Kia PV5 Passenger and the short-wheelbase VW ID. Buzz. The body sits lower than a traditional SUV, with smooth lines and a roof spoiler recalling the Espace 2 and 3. The cabin is fully glazed, an approach Renault attributes to Bauhaus architecture and to Ludwig Mies van der Rohe's Farnsworth House, with glass extending beyond a low waistline. Romain Gauvin, Renault's brand head of advanced design and concept cars, said that lets people see into the cabin when standing beside the car and lets the driver "drive with your elbows on the door".

Rear-hinged double doors without a central pillar — a detail specified in Italian coverage — open onto six individual seats on a flat floor. The seats have lacquered shells and can each rotate; the second row swivels 180 degrees to form what Renault calls a "TGV train square" with the third row. Second-row passengers get a folding tray table and a 12.3-inch headrest-mounted screen, and folding those seats creates a large table served by a remote-control console containing an air purifier, a small fridge, video game controllers and a Connect 4 game.

A pillar-to-pillar curved display, OpenR Panorama, spans 1,130 mm, alongside a central infotainment screen; both swivel on a base behind the steering wheel. The compact wheel uses steer-by-wire technology, which Stéphane Maiore, Renault's brand head of interior design, said is "free from all the physical constraints typically associated with steering". Italian coverage reports 23-inch wheels at the corners and materials including pure wool carpet, paints with 18 per cent bio-based resins and handmade coloured-straw inserts in place of leather and wood.

Renault did not confirm a production version. It hints the concept is a "contemporary retake on travel and family mobility in the electric age" that "outlines its vision for the car of the future".

items.title: BYD unveils seven-seat Atto 8 with 115 kWh battery for Europe
items.summary: BYD says the seven-seat Atto 8, its first European model with second-generation Blade batteries, will reach dealers in the first quarter of 2027 with a 115 kWh pack.
items.content_html:
AI-assisted summary — A concise view to help navigate news and sources. Learn more

BYD used the Paris auto show to introduce the Atto 8, a seven-seat battery-electric SUV that becomes the company's first European model to carry its second-generation Blade battery and its FLASH Charging system. The battery and the charging claim are the substance of the announcement. Stella Li, the company's executive vice president, said on Monday that BYD is "all about turning intelligence into reality". Affari Italiani notes that charging speed, interior space and range weigh increasingly heavily in European buyers' choices of battery-electric cars.

Both variants use a 115 kWh Blade 2.0 battery. The Design RWD has a single rear motor rated at 340 kW, reported as 456 hp by Electrek and 462 CV by Affari Italiani, delivering a claimed 0-62 mph time of eight seconds. The Excellence AWD adds a front motor for a combined 570 kW — 764 hp and 775 CV respectively — with 775 Nm of torque and a claimed 0-62 mph of 4.6 seconds. BYD gives a WLTP range of up to 405 miles (653 km) for the rear-drive version and 374 miles (602 km) for the all-wheel-drive one; the two figures are the same manufacturer claims expressed in different units.

BYD says the FLASH system charges from 10% to 80% in five minutes, from 10% to 97% in nine minutes, and from 20% to 97% in 12 minutes at temperatures as low as -30°C, and states that this is about a third of the time rival SUVs need for 10% to 80%. Affari Italiani notes that the full test conditions and the availability of the necessary infrastructure are not specified in the announcement, so the times should be read as manufacturer claims rather than as performance guaranteed at any charger.

The vehicle measures 5,040 mm long, 1,996 mm wide and 1,760 mm tall, with 270 litres of luggage space behind seven seats, 1,960 litres with the second and third rows folded, and a 136-litre front compartment. BYD says European dealers will begin selling it in the first quarter of 2027. No prices have been announced; Electrek reports that, positioned above the Ti 7 plug-in hybrid, it will likely start at slightly over £47,995 on the road in the UK.

items.title: Smart unveils electric #2 two-seater in Paris with 290 km WLTP range
items.summary: The Mercedes-Benz and Geely joint venture has revived its two-seat city car format, pricing the #2 from €19,990 in Germany, France and Italy with a 35.8 kWh LFP pack.
items.content_html:
AI-assisted summary — A concise view to help navigate news and sources. Learn more

Smart has revived its two-seat city car as an electric model, the #2, unveiled at the Paris motor show. The pitch is aimed squarely at urban mobility: a compact battery-electric vehicle for dense traffic and difficult parking, produced by the Mercedes-Benz and Geely joint venture, with design by Mercedes-Benz and industrial production in China, according to Rinnovabili and Electrek.

The #2 sits on a new platform Smart calls Electric Compact Architecture, with the battery in the floor and a 60 kW motor driving the rear wheels with 130 Nm of torque, Electrek reports. Electrek says Smart claims a first-in-class five-link rear suspension. Rinnovabili reports a 35.8 kWh lithium-iron-phosphate pack supplied by CATL and a WLTP range of up to 290 km; Electrek gives the same capacity and range. The car measures about 2.75 m, roughly five centimetres more than the EQ Fortwo, with a 6.95 m turning circle.

On DC charging, both Rinnovabili and Electrek report 10 to 80 per cent in about 20 minutes at up to 65 kW. The base Pure trim carries a 7.4 kW single-phase onboard charger taking roughly five hours for the same session, while other trims have 11 kW units, which Rinnovabili says complete it in about three hours. Electrek notes that vehicle-to-load requires a separate adapter.

Smart quotes a German starting price of €19,990 for the Pure, which Electrek says also applies in France and Italy; Blick reports a Swiss entry price of 18,300 francs. Four trims are listed, ending in a Couture Edition limited to 999 units in Europe, Electrek reports. Electrek says early orders open in Europe the day after the unveiling, with retail-partner sales preceding online ordering in the first half of 2027 and deliveries starting in 2027, while Blick reports a Swiss dealer rollout towards the end of the year. The #2 is still undergoing EU homologation and specifications could change, Electrek notes. Electrek compares the car with Renault's Twingo E-Tech, also €19,990 in Germany, with a 27.5 kWh pack and 262 km of WLTP range, and notes the Twingo offers four seats and five doors. Electrek adds that Daimler withdrew Smart from the United States and Canada in 2019.

items.title: Citroën shows electric 2CV concept, targeting 2028 launch near €15,000
items.summary: The French brand's Paris Motor Show prototype revives a 1948 design as a compact battery model, with production planned for 2028 and technical details still unpublished.
items.content_html:
AI-assisted summary — A concise view to help navigate news and sources. Learn more

Citroën unveiled the 2 CV Concept at the Paris Motor Show, which Blick dates to 12–18 October 2026, as an electric city car it intends to build in Europe by 2028 with an indicative starting price of about €15,000. Ámbito Financiero links the project to European initiatives encouraging smaller, cheaper electric cars, and Affari Italiani notes Citroën's reference to a European small-car framework it calls E-Car. No battery capacity, range, power output or charging time has been published; Affari Italiani reports that price, timing and series specifications remain to be confirmed.

The concept measures 3.76 metres — shorter than the original's 3.83 metres, per Blick, and about 20 centimetres shorter by Liberty Times's account. Affari Italiani and Electrek report a target weight near one tonne, and Ámbito Financiero and Affari Italiani say the model would sit between the Ami and the C3. Blick quotes Stellantis chief designer Gilles Vidal saying the concept already matches the production car externally, and Citroën chief executive Xavier Chardon saying the revival reinterprets the original's simplicity, accessibility and freedom rather than copying it — a line Ámbito Financiero also attributes to him.

Technical disclosure is thin. Citroën has published no motor output, battery capacity, range or charging times; Liberty Times judges that the low price makes high performance or very long range unlikely. Blick reports a company statement promising only an "everyday-appropriate range" from a "low-cost battery", and labels its own 200 to 300 kilometre estimate as speculation rather than a manufacturer figure.

Inside, Ámbito Financiero and Affari Italiani describe a cylindrical structure replacing the conventional dashboard, carrying a single-spoke wheel and an eight-inch square touchscreen with comic-style graphics. A removable basket substitutes for the centre console, door panels include egg holders echoing the original's basket-of-eggs brief noted by Liberty Times and Hamshahri Online, and a portable Radioën radio detaches for use as a speaker. Advanced Comfort seats appear, and Ámbito Financiero reports Citroën is still weighing whether to keep a manually opening fabric roof.

Histories of the original diverge. Liberty Times says more than 3.8 million were built between 1948 and 1990; Blick gives 5.1 million — 3.9 million saloons and 1.2 million vans — for 1949 to 1990. Wheel sizes differ too: Liberty Times cites 19-inch wheels, while Ámbito Financiero and Affari Italiani describe 18-inch steel wheels. Liberty Times expects a production debut at the 2028 Paris show; Blick says Stellantis wants the car on the road within two years.

items.title: Mitsubishi's ASX VR-e electric SUV adds 459 hp all-wheel-drive variant
items.summary: The battery-electric compact SUV is built in Taiwan by Foxconn from the Pininfarina-styled Foxtron Bria, but Australian prices, range and charging details remain unpublished.
items.content_html:
AI-assisted summary — A concise view to help navigate news and sources. Learn more

Mitsubishi is readying a battery-electric compact SUV, the ASX VR-e, whose most powerful version puts a motor on each axle. The model sits in the electric-vehicle and battery strand of sustainable-mobility coverage on the terms the sources establish: it is specified with a 57.7 kWh lithium-ion battery across the range, while Mitsubishi has not published homologated Australian range, charging times or maximum DC charging power.

The range-topping GSR variant pairs a front motor with a rear one, giving all-wheel drive. Radio Mitre puts its output at 465 CV and its 0-100 km/h time at 3.9 seconds. Electrek, describing the same all-wheel-drive version, reports 459 hp (342 kW) and roughly 516 lb-ft (700 Nm) of torque. The two outlets express the peak figure in different units rather than offering competing measurements.

The three remaining versions — LS, Aspire and Exceed — use a single motor on the rear axle. Radio Mitre reports 232 CV, 350 Nm and a 0-100 km/h time of 6.8 seconds for them, but its wording is collective: the source does not make clear whether those figures apply to each variant or to the three taken together.

The vehicle is not built by Mitsubishi. Foxconn, the Taiwanese technology manufacturer, builds it under its Foxtron automotive brand, and the model derives from the Foxtron Bria, whose design Radio Mitre attributes to Pininfarina. Mitsubishi contributes the name, the dealership network and after-sales service.

Market status differs between the accounts. Electrek states the ASX VR-e is currently on sale in the Taiwanese and Australian markets; Radio Mitre describes an Australian debut for which the local subsidiary has not published a price, a final equipment list or an exact sale date. Radio Mitre uses the Toyota Corolla Cross as a size reference and notes that it needs more than nine seconds to reach 100 km/h, while Electrek observes that the new model delivers more power and more torque than the UK-only, combustion-engined Lancer Evo X FQ-440 MR, rated at 440 hp.

items.title: Volkswagen’s ID. Tiguan to succeed the ID.4 and ID.5 in Europe
items.summary: The all-electric SUV will take over from the ID.4 and ID.5, offering two battery sizes, three drivetrains and a WLTP range of up to 372 miles.
items.content_html:
AI-assisted summary — A concise view to help navigate news and sources. Learn more

Volkswagen has unveiled the ID. Tiguan, an all-electric SUV that will replace the ID.4 and ID.5 in its line-up. It follows the ID. Polo and ID. Cross as what the company calls a “True Volkswagen”; more than 950,000 ID.4 and ID.5 cars have been sold since 2021, Electrek reports, so the change affects an established line-up. Thomas Schäfer, Volkswagen’s chief executive, said the Tiguan is its best-selling model worldwide and that the ID. Tiguan “brings these two success stories together”.

Electrek lists two battery packs and three drivetrains: a rear-wheel-drive version with 140 kW (190 PS) and a 58 kWh battery; a rear-wheel-drive version with 210 kW (286 PS) and a 77 kWh battery; and a 220 kW (299 PS) 4MOTION all-wheel-drive variant with 77 kWh. The Independent gives the same three as 187bhp, 282bhp and 295bhp. Electrek reports a WLTP range of up to 372 miles (600 km), a figure it presents as a new benchmark for Volkswagen’s electric SUVs in Europe; The Independent quotes a maximum claimed range of 373 miles. Towing reaches 2,000 kg with the 77 kWh battery and about 1,800 kg with the 58 kWh pack, according to Electrek.

The styling abandons the ID.4’s aerodynamic profile for a boxier SUV shape, with flush door handles giving way to pull-style items. Inside are a 10-inch Digital Cockpit and a 15-inch centre display, plus an optional 12-inch passenger screen that The Independent calls a first for a European Volkswagen. Physical buttons return below the centre display and on the steering wheel; a Retro mode reproduces the Mk4 Golf’s instruments, and a virtual garage holds six classic models.

Electrek reports that the car will launch in Germany and several other European markets on 13 October, without stating a year, at prices starting from 42,695 euros across four trims — Trend, Life, Style and R-Line. European sales run through early 2027, after which the model replaces the ID.4 in North America, where prices and other details will be announced later; The Independent places the replacement of the ID.4 and ID.5 in early 2027.

Assessment of the car remains provisional. The Independent reports that its electric vehicles editor drove a pre-production version and describes comfort as a marked improvement over the ID.4, with a controlled ride and well-weighted steering. The model is not yet on sale.

items.title: BYD's Tang Line Gains Five-Seat Interior as Great Tang Nears Europe
items.summary: BYD has revealed the interior of its five-seat third-generation Tang, while the larger Great Tang has recorded three consecutive months above 10,000 Chinese sales and executives point to early 2027 for Europe.
items.content_html:
AI-assisted summary — A concise view to help navigate news and sources. Learn more

BYD has shown the interior of the third-generation Tang, a five-seat electric SUV in its Dynasty line, while its larger stablemate, the Great Tang, continues to sell in volume in China and is being considered for a European arrival. Both sit at the centre of the company's electric-vehicle programme: they rely on BYD's latest Blade Batteries and Flash Charging technology, the battery and charging elements that tie the Dynasty range to the wider move towards electrified road transport.

The technical pitch rests on charging speed and on range measured on China's CLTC cycle. BYD says the third-generation Tang can charge from 10% to 70% in as little as five minutes using Blade Batteries 2.0 and Flash Charging; it says the car will be offered with 88.682 kWh and 105.792 kWh battery packs. The Great Tang uses a 1,000-volt electrical architecture, with the Italian outlet Vaielettrico reporting a 10% to 70% charge in five minutes and 10% to 97% in nine. Its most powerful electric version claims up to 950 km of CLTC range. The third-generation Tang is listed at 730 km, 830 km or 850 km on the same cycle, depending on configuration. The three-row Great Tang measures 5.26 metres long on a 3,130 mm wheelbase; the five-seat third-generation Tang is 5,045 mm long on a 2,950 mm wheelbase. Neither article states whether the quoted battery capacities are gross or net figures.

In China, the Great Tang's commercial debut in mid-June was preceded by a pre-sale phase in which orders passed 100,000 within two weeks and exceeded 150,000 before sales opened, according to Vaielettrico. September brought 13,010 units, taking cumulative sales past 40,200 and marking three consecutive months above 10,000. Electrek reports that BYD has yet to reveal prices for the third-generation Tang, and notes that the full-size Great Tang starts at 239,900 yuan.

Viewed from Europe, the more consequential question is timing. BYD executives have indicated early 2027 as a possible window for the model's arrival in international markets including Europe, though specifications and pricing adapted to those markets remain to be verified. That is an indication rather than a confirmed schedule. In Italy, Vaielettrico reports, the brand recorded 5,161 registrations in September for a 3.7% share, which it puts at a 108.9% increase over the same month of 2025, with 41,697 registrations across the first nine months.

items.title: Porsche Confirms All-Electric 718 Lineup for 2028 as 911 Stays Combustion
items.summary: Porsche will build its Boxster and Cayman sports cars only as battery-electric models, with 2028 its first full production year, while the 911 keeps its combustion engine.
items.content_html:
AI-assisted summary — A concise view to help navigate news and sources. Learn more

Porsche has confirmed that its 718 family — the Boxster convertible and the Cayman hardtop — will be built only as battery-electric cars, with 2028 named as the first full year of production. The announcement came at an investor presentation that the Italian outlet Vaielettrico identifies as the Capital Markets Day 2026. Petrol versions of the two models left production in 2025. For the electric-vehicle and battery sector, the decision turns less on the badge than on the pack: where a battery sits in a sports car shapes both the driving position and the distribution of weight, and Porsche's answer departs from the floor-mounted norm.

According to a ride-along on Porsche's Weissach test track reported by Car and Driver and cited by both outlets, the 718 mounts its battery behind the seats rather than beneath the cabin floor. Most electric cars place the pack low in the vehicle. Porsche's alternative is intended to preserve a low seating position and to reproduce the balance of the outgoing mid-engined versions, whose engine sat behind the occupants. The petrol Boxster carried a 59.8 per cent rear weight bias, while the electric car is reported at 55.2 per cent.

Car and Driver called the layout unique, a description Electrek disputed, noting that the Tesla Roadster used a comparable arrangement with roughly 35/65 front-to-rear distribution. Electrek welcomed the commitment to an electric 718 after what it described as Porsche's back-and-forth on electrification, and said the company had recently booked a $6 billion loss that the outlet attributed to its resistance to electrification. The same article noted that Porsche also plans a new SUV with petrol and plug-in hybrid power.

On the 911, chief executive Michael Leiters said during the presentation that the model will "never" be electric. Vaielettrico, which describes Leiters as a former Ferrari chief executive, read the remark as excluding a fully electric 911 within the strategic horizon set by management, while leaving room for hybrid systems that retain a combustion engine. Electrek took a different view, predicting that time will prove him wrong.

items.title: Autotorino's ATFlow to Handle Italian Distribution of GAC's AION Electric Cars
items.summary: The Chinese carmaker's two lithium-iron-phosphate models reach Italian buyers through the Autotorino subsidiary ATFlow, priced from €25,750 for the compact UT and €33,880 for the SUV.
items.content_html:
AI-assisted summary — A concise view to help navigate news and sources. Learn more

GAC, the Chinese carmaker based in Guangzhou, has begun selling two battery-electric models in Italy: the compact AION UT and the SUV AION V, both using lithium-iron-phosphate batteries. Italian distribution is handled by ATFlow, a company wholly controlled by Gruppo Autotorino. The two models compete in the compact and SUV electric segments, as Adnkronos describes them, and the battery capacity, WLTP range and charging details reported for them are the parameters that place them within the electric-vehicle and charging part of the mobility picture.

Both cars use a 150 kW motor, which the Italian outlet Adnkronos gives as 204 CV, driving the front wheels. The UT carries a 60 kWh net LFP battery and a declared WLTP combined range of up to 430 km; GAC quotes 0-100 km/h in 7.3 seconds and a 160 km/h top speed. The AION V pairs the same-rated 150 kW motor with an LFP battery given as 75.26 kWh by Adnkronos and 75 kWh by Vaielettrico. Neither source labels the V's capacity as gross or net, whereas Adnkronos describes the UT's as net. The V's declared WLTP combined range is 510 km, with DC charging up to 180 kW; GAC declares under 25 minutes for 10 to 80 per cent, and the car offers vehicle-to-load output up to 3.3 kW.

Adnkronos reports that the UT starts at €25,750 in Premium trim and €26,750 in Luxury, both with the same motorisation and battery. The AION V starts at €33,880 in Premium form and €34,880 in Luxury, with the Premium including a panoramic roof, electric tailgate, heated and ventilated front seats and heated rear seats, while Luxury adds eight-point massage for the front seats. Both models carry an 8.8-inch instrument display and a 14.6-inch central screen with wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto and online navigation.

In a first drive published by Vaielettrico, conducted on city and extra-urban roads, the V measured 4.60 metres in length with a 430-litre boot, rising above 1,600 litres with the rear seats folded. The outlet declined to draw conclusions from the consumption figure it recorded, saying the distance covered was too short to be representative. It reported that the V holds five Euro NCAP stars and level 2 driver assistance, and that it accelerates from 0 to 100 km/h in just under 8 seconds.

items.title: BMW's New iX4 Electric Coupé-SUV Combines 828 km WLTP Range With 400 kW Charging
items.summary: The third model in BMW's Neue Klasse electric line-up replaces the X4, pairing dual-motor all-wheel drive with an 800-volt architecture and sales due from March 2027.
items.content_html:
AI-assisted summary — A concise view to help navigate news and sources. Learn more

BMW has unveiled the iX4, an all-electric coupé-SUV and the third model in its Neue Klasse electric family after the iX3 and i3. It replaces the discontinued X4 with electric propulsion only and is due on sale in March 2027. The launch belongs to the electric-vehicle strand of sustainable mobility through its battery, charging and range specifications.

Two variants arrive first with all-wheel drive, each using one electric motor per axle. Vaielettrico reports net battery capacities of 82.6 kWh for the iX4 40 xDrive and 108.7 kWh for the 50 xDrive; Electrek gives 112.2 kWh for the 50 xDrive without stating whether that figure is gross or net. BMW quotes 828 km on the WLTP cycle for the 50 xDrive, the launch model, and Electrek also cites an estimated 428 miles on the US basis. Vaielettrico lists 638 km WLTP for the 40 xDrive and 777 km for the M60 xDrive.

The two outlets report differing charging limits. Vaielettrico assigns a maximum DC rate of 400 kW to the 50 xDrive and 300 kW to the 40 xDrive, while Electrek says both models charge at up to 400 kW, citing an 800-volt architecture. Their ten-minute range gains differ too, reflecting different test-cycle references: Vaielettrico reports up to 387 km for the 50 xDrive under favourable conditions, Electrek up to 184 miles, roughly 296 km, for both models. Both report bidirectional charging, which Vaielettrico says lets the car power external devices, subject to market specifications and infrastructure.

Output figures are stated in different units. Vaielettrico gives the 50 xDrive 345 kW, or 469 CV, and the M60 450 kW, or 612 CV, with a 0-100 km/h time of 3.9 seconds and a 240 km/h top speed. Electrek reports 468 hp and 475 lb-ft for the 50 xDrive with a 0-60 mph time of 4.7 seconds, and 603 hp and 645 lb-ft for the M60. Vaielettrico says orders for the 40 and 50 xDrive are indicated to open in October, with the Italian price list still undefined. Electrek puts US pricing for the 50 xDrive at $66,200 before a $1,495 destination fee, with M60 pricing to come. Production is at BMW's Debrecen plant in Hungary.
